title: The Longest Animal Ever Found Isn't One Animal
subject: siphonophore

scenes.text: The longest animal ever filmed is not a whale. And it isn't one animal.
Off Western Australia, a robot sub found a glowing string about 150 feet long.
That is twice the length of a blue whale, and thin as a broomstick.
It is a siphonophore: thousands of clones joined in a chain, each with its own job.
Some feed, some swim, some sting. They coil into a spiral to trap fish.
So the longest animal on Earth is really a team that never separates.

description:
The longest animal ever filmed is not a whale, and it isn't even one animal.
A siphonophore off Western Australia stretched about 150 feet, made of thousands of joined clones.
Would you call a team that never separates one animal?
first_comment: One animal or a thousand? Where would you draw the line?
